title: leadline-microcopy-labs
body:
Purpose: quick lab to generate distinct headline + microcopy families for homepage and product landing experiments. Goal is to find a short sequence that resonates with engineers and platform teams while surfacing what actually matters to buying motion: predictable unit economics, low-latency SLAs, and drop-in consistency across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.

Notes/context (informal):
- We need copy that speaks to engineers first — they are the ones building, prototyping, and approving infra buys. But page should surface enterprise signals for procurement.
- Avoid generic "fast and cheap" language; instead emphasize what’s controlled (latency budgets, cost per token, predictable throughput).
- Provide explicit expected outcomes (e.g., "reduce per-token cost by X% for chat workloads") where we can, but keep hero microcopy lean.
- Tests should clearly map to metric: sign-up conversion, SDK install, dedicated interest form completions.

Hero families (6 distinct approaches) - raw variants to A/B: 
1) Predictability-first
- Headline: "Inference you can budget for"
- Subhead: "Consistent latency, predictable unit costs, and rollouts you control — across hosted, reserved, or private deployments."
- CTA A: "Estimate my cost" | CTA B: "Try with free credits"
- Hook for engineers (micro): "Pin a model version. Set a latency SLO. We’ll handle routing and fallbacks."
- Why this might work: speaks to procurement + engineers who hate surprise bills.

2) Engineering assurance
- Headline: "Ship LLM features without rebuilding inference"
- Subhead: "A runtime and control plane built for production: batching, KV caching, and automatic fallbacks so your app stays fast."
- CTA: "Start a deployable demo"
- Microcopy: "Deploy in minutes, optimize cost later with recommended batching profiles."

3) Cost-performance tradeoff (granular)
- Headline: "Tune cost and latency per-route"
- Subhead: "Choose routing policies, quantization profiles, and batch windows by endpoint — measurable savings, predictable latency."
- CTA: "See optimization examples"
- Micro: "Per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns."

4) Trust & reliability (enterprise signal)
- Headline: "SLA-backed inference for customer-facing apps"
- Subhead: "Dedicated capacity, observability, and fallbacks so you can meet SLAs under load."
- CTA: "Request enterprise terms"
- Micro: "Can integrate with your KMS and VPC."

5) Developer velocity (productivity)
- Headline: "From prototype to production — same API"
- Subhead: "One SDK, multiple deployment modes. Keep code unchanged while you scale from dev keys to reserved capacity."
- CTA: "Get the SDK"
- Micro: "Examples: chat, RAG, embeddings — copy-paste to switch between hosted and private."

6) Differentiated technical claim (runtime + kernel)
- Headline: "Inference optimized for real workloads"
- Subhead: "Smart kernel selection, continuous batching, and KV cache reuse for long-context and multi-turn apps."
- CTA: "View benchmarks"
- Micro: "Benchmarks tailored to conversation length distributions and hardware tiers."

Microcopy experiments (small swappable pieces):
- CTA button text variations: "Estimate my cost" / "Try free credits" / "Run a demo" / "Get the SDK" / "Request enterprise terms"
- Short form field microcopy: "Expected monthly tokens" -> adjust to "Typical monthly requests (messages)" for product clarity
- Tooltip lines: "Automatic fallback: when capacity tight, route to compatible variant" vs. "Automatic fallback: keep requests flowing with degraded-but-safe models"
- Error state copy: "We’re retrying on a warm node — this won’t count against usage" (risky — legal check)

Competitive notes (quick, non-exhaustive):
- Direct vs managed: prospects often weigh "control" (self-host) vs "speed/cost" (managed). We need to own the middle: managed runtime with deployment flexibility.
- Observability is a differentiator: competitors often surface throughput or latency curves but not token-level economics + per-route dashboards — push this.
- Pricing signal: buyers respond to tangible metrics (cost per 1k tokens for chat, cost per 1k embeddings). Wherever possible, map copy to an example workload with numbers in a linked example page.

Prioritization matrix for initial experiments (MVP):
- Test A (2-week): Predictability-first hero vs Engineering assurance hero. Measure: hero CTA CTR, sign-ups/day, SDK installs.
- Test B (2-week): CTA variations on Predictability-first: "Estimate my cost" vs "Try free credits". Measure: lead form starts, conversion to sign-up.
- Test C (4-week): Microcopy for error/timeout messaging in docs and SDK landing page — measure reduction in support tickets for timeouts.

Success criteria (hypotheses):
- If headline explicitly mentions "predictable" or "budget" we hypothesize +15% lift in enterprise interest forms (baseline: 1.8% -> target 2.1%).
- If CTA is "Estimate my cost" vs generic "Start free" expect higher MQL quality (fewer spam signups, more reserved-capacity trials).

Open questions / to resolve:
- Legal check on usage microcopy that implies credit/refund behavior ("won’t count against usage").
- Can marketing provide 1-2 realistic cost examples we can use on-page (not proprietary)?
- Do we want to show competitor comparisons directly on product page or keep soft allusions? (ops: keep soft for first tests)

Next steps / action items:
- Priya to wireframe Predictability-first hero + lead form (ETA 72h).
- Diego to run quick benchmark snippets (quantized model vs unquantized) and provide micro numbers for the "See optimization examples" page (ETA 5 days).
- Samir to draft analytics plan for A/B tests and final KPI definitions (ETA 3 days).
- Go-to-market sync: decide on two headline families to run in next sprint (deadline: next Wed).

Notes to self / crumbs:
- Keep hero microcopy under 8 words where possible.
- Use verbs that imply operational control: "pin", "route", "set" rather than abstract nouns.
- Avoid overpromising on "cost savings" — prefer "optimize" or "reduce by up to" with a clear example page link.

Rough taglines/snippets (one-liners to steal into CTAs or cards):
- "Predictable inference, no surprise bills."
- "Same API from prototype to private cloud."
- "Tune cost per route, keep latency budgets."
- "Observability that ties quality to cost."

End of doc — rough, iterative. This is a working lab file: please add notes inline and drop additional microcopy variants.
